original.target_description: Experiment 1: main effect of stimulus velocity on reaction time to colour or luminance change, two-way repeated measures ANOVA across velocity and type of change.

n.sample_role: Observers contributing averaged reaction times to the repeated measures ANOVA; participant count, not trial count.
n.exclusions: Only RTs over 100 ms and below 1000 ms included; 35 misses and 769 anticipatory responses excluded. No participant exclusion reported.
n.quote: Seven observers, four women (20, 21, 22, and 30 years) ... and three men (20, 21, and 22 years), with normal or cor- ... rected-to-normal vision participated in the experiment. ... Only RTs over ... 100 ms and below 1000 ms were included.

es.location: Printed p. 1850 (PDF p. 3), §2.2, velocity main effect.
es.quote: cant eVects of velocity [F (5, 12) D 343.7; p < .0001]

p.location: Printed p. 1850 (PDF p. 3), §2.2, same velocity main effect.
p.quote: cant eVects of velocity [F (5, 12) D 343.7; p < .0001]

replication.target_description: Single unnumbered experiment: effect of stimulus velocity (0, 4.4, 17.6 degrees/s) on reaction time to coloration change; seven participants; repeated-measures ANOVA.

n.location: p. 2, Materials and methods—Participants; p. 4, Results—Reaction Times
n.quote: Seven participants (six females and one male, aged 20–25) took part in this experiment.
n.sample_role: Participants in the repeated-measures reaction-time ANOVA; seven participants described, with participant count corroborated by F(2,12).
n.exclusions: RTs over 1000 ms and below 100 ms excluded: 16 misses and 146 anticipated responses out of 2100 responses; no participant exclusion reported.

es.location: p. 4, Results—Reaction Times, velocity main effect

p.location: p. 4, Results—Reaction Times, same velocity main effect

reported_success.quote: Psychophysical results replicate the findings from the previous study showing decreased RTs to coloration changes with increase of velocity of the color changing stimulus.

notes:
Replication source title verified. The 2014 article reports one unnumbered experiment; treated as the supplied Experiment 1. Original acquisition: DOI route inaccessible; OpenAlex identifies publisher PDF, which returned HTTP 403; promising author-dissertation repository route timed out. No original statistics inferred from replication citations.
Source follow-up: Published article, Vision Research 46 (2006), pp. 1848–1855; supplied title/authors/DOI match. PDF pages 2–3 rendered and inspected. Canonical text quotes preserve eVects and D (rendered PDF shows effects and equals sign); numeric F, degrees of freedom and p-bound verified visually. Reported degrees of freedom retained as printed, without correcting them. No replication verdict extracted for an original-only target. Explicit ellipses mark interleaved column omissions in the sample quotation.
